Serve the parish

There are many small ways to help make parish life welcoming, beautiful and possible. Most take an hour, and none of them needs an introduction.

All parish ministries →
Welcome ministry
Greet visitors in the narthex and make sure a newcomer does not have to navigate a first Liturgy alone. Greeters serve on Sunday mornings today; a trained welcome ministry is one of the proposals in this draft.
Proposed
Kids' Corner
Keep the activity supplies in order and prepare an occasional saint's-day or feast-day activity for the children during fellowship. This is the ministry the corner described above would need in order to exist.
Proposed
Coffee hour
Host a Sunday, or help another household with theirs. Two families sharing one Sunday is a good way to do it the first time.
The Agape Meal
Bring food, set up the hall, serve, or stay behind and clear away. The half nobody sees is the half most worth offering.
Setup & cleanup
Lay out the parish hall before a gathering, or put it back afterwards. Half an hour, on a Sunday you are here anyway.
Proposed
Parish events
Feast-day celebrations, the Greek Festival and special parish gatherings — every one of them is put on by parishioners.
Charitable outreach
Serving our neighbours and the wider community. Most of it happens through the Ladies' Philoptochos Society.
Missions
Supporting Orthodox mission work at home and abroad. Nothing is organised at parish level yet, and this card is here to ask whether it should be.
Proposed
Something else?
If what you can offer is not on this list, tell the parish office what you would like to help with. They will find the right person to put you in touch with.
Proposed — for Fr. John's review

Four of the nine above do not exist today. They are shown as proposals rather than as sign-up links, because a link to a ministry nobody runs yet costs the person who follows it more than the blank space would. Each becomes a real link the moment the parish decides who leads it.
